Print on Letter at 100%. The last page is the drill list for the coach: questions only, no answers.

Robot Design: the questions judges might ask

5 minutes of questions after our 5-minute explanation. The judges choose who answers, so read every part, not just yours.

ShortTwo or three sentences, then stop. The judge asks more if they want more.
Honest"I don't know, but my teammate built that" is a good answer. A made-up one falls apart at the follow-up.
Your wordsKnow the idea, not the words. Orange answers need our own facts: find them before practice.

Strategy

10
What is the robo taxi?
One trip carries the attachment and the keystone to the right.
Follow-up: What if the keystone falls off?
21
Why this order of runs?
Left first, close first, then the robo taxi.
Follow-up: What if the first run fails?
22
Which mission did you skip?
Lucky Leaves: far, partly luck, 10 or 20 points.
Follow-up: What would make it worth doing?
30
Whose idea was the robo taxi?
The true answer.
Follow-up: How did the team decide?

Robot

1
Why is your robot shaped like that?
A flat box squares up on a wall, so every run starts the same way.
Follow-up: What if it starts crooked?
2
Why those wheels?
The designs that slipped all used blue SPIKE wheels, so we use grippy ones.
Follow-up: How did you check yours don't slip?
3
Where is the robot's weight?
Team to measure: say where the heaviest part is, and that you checked for a wobble.
Follow-up: How did you test it?
4
How does the BOXOR frame move the arm?
Two bevel gears turn the movement through 90 degrees.
Follow-up: What is the gear ratio?
5
Why gravity mounting?
One move to swap. Last season, swaps were slow.
Follow-up: Has one ever fallen off?
6
How long does a swap take?
Give the measured time.
Follow-up: How did you measure it?
7
Why a push instead of a motor?
Motors can go wrong. A push can't.
Follow-up: When did you need a motor anyway?
8
Why is the attachment on the back?
Team to agree.
Follow-up: Why do your distances have minus signs?
9
What would you change with more time?
Take the play out of the arm gears, maybe with a rubber band.
Follow-up: How would you know it worked?
19
How does the arm know where it is?
It starts on its stopper, and the code calls that zero.
Follow-up: What if it doesn't start there?

Code

12
Why Python?
Last year's Python, more control, and git shows every change.
Follow-up: What was hard about switching?
16
What if something goes wrong in a run?
More than 45 degrees off, it stops. Over 8 seconds, it gives up and goes on.
Follow-up: Why stop?
17
How are distances accurate?
We asked for 180 cm and got 179, so we scale by 179/180.
Follow-up: What if you change the wheels?
18
What did you reuse from last year?
drive_cm. We changed the wheel size from 88 mm to 62.4 mm.
Follow-up: Why did that number matter?
20
What's the cleverest thing in your code?
The arm lifts while the robot drives home, by leaving out await.
Follow-up: How much time does it save?

Sensors

11
How does it drive straight?
It reads the gyro every 15 ms and steers back, harder the further off.
Follow-up: What stops it wiggling?
13
What does face(90) do?
Turns to point 90 degrees from where we started.
Follow-up: Why not just turn 90?
14
What is PID?
P pushes harder when far off, I pushes more when stuck, D eases off when closing in fast.
Follow-up: Which parts does drive_cm use?
15
Why not the colour sensors?
They're plugged in, but only the gyroscope steers. It works everywhere on the mat, not just near a line.
Follow-up: Would a sensor have helped anywhere?

Iteration and team

23
How reliable is your robot?
Give the 10-run numbers.
Follow-up: Which run is weakest?
24
How do you test a change?
Change one thing, run it 10 times, compare.
Follow-up: Give an example.
25
What broke, and how did you fix it?
One fix story, four parts: problem, how we found out, what we changed, result.
Follow-up: How did you find the cause?
26
What didn't work?
Pushing the arm into its stopper lifted the attachment, so we dropped that idea.
Follow-up: What did you do instead?
27
How do you know a fix helped?
A number before and a number after.
Follow-up: What if it only helped sometimes?
28
Who built and coded what?
Each member answers for themselves.
Follow-up: Explain your teammate's part.
29
How did you share the work?
Roles, and we swapped so everyone tried each.
Follow-up: What happened when you disagreed?
31
What did you learn?
One real lesson each.
Follow-up: How will you use it next season?
32
What are you most proud of?
Said like you mean it.
Follow-up: Why that one?

Question drill: all 32

The coach reads a question and points at anyone. Answer in two or three sentences, then stop. Tick a box each time it is answered well.
